title: Coverings of semi-representable objects are stable under composition and base change
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ the category of semi-representable objects over $X$, with its coverings [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. (1) If $a:K\to L$ and $b:L\to M$ are coverings in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, then $b\circ a:K\to M$ is a covering. (2) If $a:K\to L$ is a covering and $c:L'\to L$ is any morphism of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, then the fibre product $L'\times_LK$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ exists, and its projection $L'\times_LK\to L'$ is a covering, where $L'\times_LK$ is the fibre product of [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (2) (applied to $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$): for $K=\{K_i\}_{i\in I}$, $L=\{L_j\}_{j\in J}$, $L'=\{L'_l\}_{l\in J'}$, $a=(\alpha,a_i)$, $c=(\gamma,c_l)$, it is the family $\{L'_l\times_{c_l,L_{\gamma(l)},a_i}K_i\}_{(l,i)\in J'\times I,\ \gamma(l)=\alpha(i)}$, and the projection has index map $(l,i)\mapsto l$ and components the first projections.

proof.text: Notation. By [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (3), a morphism $(\alpha,f_i):\{U_i\}_{i\in I}\to\{V_j\}_{j\in J}$ of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is a covering iff for every $j\in J$ the family $\{f_i:U_i\to V_j\}_{i\in I,\,\alpha(i)=j}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$, and by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] a covering family of $X_{\Et}$ is a family of etale morphisms (between objects etale over $X$, the morphisms being $X$-morphisms) which is jointly surjective onto its target. Composition in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ is $(\beta,b_j)\circ(\alpha,a_i)=(\beta\circ\alpha,(b_{\alpha(i)}\circ a_i)_{i})$ [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (1).

Proof of (1) (Stacks: 'immediate from the axioms of a site', written out). Write $K=\{K_i\}_{i\in I}$, $L=\{L_j\}_{j\in J}$, $M=\{M_n\}_{n\in N}$, $a=(\alpha,a_i)$, $b=(\beta,b_j)$. Fix $n\in N$. Since $b$ is a covering, $\{b_j:L_j\to M_n\}_{j\in J,\,\beta(j)=n}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms; since $a$ is a covering, for each such $j$ the family $\{a_i:K_i\to L_j\}_{i\in I,\,\alpha(i)=j}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] (with $T=M_n$, the $f$'s the $b_j$ and, over $L_j$, the $g$'s the $a_i$ with $\alpha(i)=j$), the family $\{b_j\circ a_i:K_i\to M_n\}$ indexed by the pairs $(j,i)$ with $\beta(j)=n$, $\alpha(i)=j$ consists of etale morphisms and is jointly surjective. The map $i\mapsto(\alpha(i),i)$ is a bijection from $\{i\in I:\beta(\alpha(i))=n\}$ onto this set of pairs (inverse $(j,i)\mapsto i$), under which $b_j\circ a_i=b_{\alpha(i)}\circ a_i$ is the $i$-th component of $b\circ a$ (step 1); the composites are $X$-morphisms between objects of $X_{\Et}$. Hence $\{b_{\alpha(i)}\circ a_i:K_i\to M_n\}_{i:\,\beta\alpha(i)=n}$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$ for every $n$, i.e. $b\circ a$ is a covering.

proof.text: Proof of (2), the fibre product. Write $K,L,L',a,c$ as in the statement. $X_{\Et}$ has a final object $\mathrm{id}_X$ and fibre products, computed as fibre products of schemes [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (2) applied to $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$, the family $P=\{P_{(l,i)}\}$, $P_{(l,i)}=L'_l\times_{c_l,L_{\gamma(l)},a_i}K_i$ for $(l,i)\in J'\times I$ with $\gamma(l)=\alpha(i)$, with the projections $p'=((l,i)\mapsto l,\ \mathrm{pr}_1)$ to $L'$ and $p=((l,i)\mapsto i,\ \mathrm{pr}_2)$ to $K$, is a fibre product $L'\times_LK$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$; each $P_{(l,i)}$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre product, an object of $X_{\Et}$.

proof.text: Proof of (2), the covering. Fix $l\in J'$ and put $j=\gamma(l)$. The members of $P$ over $l$ are indexed by $\{(l,i): \alpha(i)=j\}$, i.e. by $\{i\in I:\alpha(i)=j\}$, and the corresponding components of $p'$ are the first projections $\mathrm{pr}_1:L'_l\times_{c_l,L_j,a_i}K_i\to L'_l$. Since $a$ is a covering, $\{a_i:K_i\to L_j\}_{\alpha(i)=j}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] (with $Y=L_j$, $V_i=K_i$, $g=c_l:L'_l\to L_j$), the projections $L'_l\times_{L_j}K_i\to L'_l$, $\alpha(i)=j$, are etale and jointly surjective; they are $X$-morphisms between objects of $X_{\Et}$ (step 3). So for every $l\in J'$ the family of components of $p'$ over $l$ is a covering family of $X_{\Et}$, i.e. $p':L'\times_LK\to L'$ is a covering [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object] (3). (This is the Stacks requirement that the morphisms of a covering are representable: in $X_{\Et}$ every fibre product exists.)
